finding: The selected Reader Index Update points the reader link to docs/reference/validation-report.md. The unselected conditional rule in specs/export-retention.md makes that exposure an artifact export that must follow the 30-day ADR 0005 retention only if the target is a generated artifact; if the target is manually maintained, the rule does not apply. The complete request gives only the existence and H1 identity of that target and never states whether it is generated or manually maintained, so whether the retention obligation applies is unknown. The selected ADR Evaluation concludes that no ADR is needed without addressing this fact.

The selected Requirements describe one routine, one-time edit of a link in docs/readers/index.md, and the spec calls it a 'routine edit'. A one-time edit of a named file is an operation, not durable product behavior or contract, so under the long-term specification boundary it belongs in issue or Agent guidance and not in this governing spec. As selected, the requirement defines a future document output rather than an input requirement that the issue implements.

The subject lists the Reader Index Update as delivered, but the Acceptance criteria contain no check for it; the only acceptance item covers public lifecycle behavior and source-reviewed internal strategies. The selected reader-index requirement assigns its pre-publication verification (old target absent, new target present exactly once, H1 identity matched) to a 'Documentation owner' that no Input defines. The deliverable therefore has no defined owner and no completion condition that the issue can verify.

The selected retention requirement sets retentionDays to 30 and passes it to persist, which the spec says 'consumes' the value. None of the persistence steps (preconditions, temporary baseline write, tracked commit) uses, records or enforces it, and the Testing Decisions exclude retention from public tests. The 30-day retention of successful tracked artifacts therefore has no defined durable effect and no verifiable behavior, so it cannot be implemented or checked from the selected text.

The selected parser requirement selects a single forward pass instead of rescanning each field, while preserving error ordering. The architecture fixes the order as UTF-8, JSON syntax, root object, requestId, checks, then entry checks, and requires only the first invalid field to be reported. In a single pass, a later UTF-8 or JSON syntax failure can be seen only after an earlier schema failure, but the requirement does not say how that precedence is kept. The Testing Decisions cover invalid UTF-8, invalid JSON and invalid schema only as separate inputs, so the preserved ordering is not verifiable from the selected tests.

The protected read is authorized only by operation: the Policy shape is {policyId, allowedOperations}, and the Decision is made 'only by operation'. The Facts also carry resourceId, and an allowed decision passes the caller-supplied request.resourceId directly as the source of readArtifact. No requirement says which artifacts the policy protects or constrains resourceId, so any operation in allowedOperations can read any source that the Reader accepts. The selected Scope describes this as a protected artifact read, but the selected text does not define what is protected.

The Design Rationale chooses to re-run policy evaluation on every protected artifact read and accepts the added latency. It names no rejected alternative, such as evaluating once per verified principal or operation, and gives no reason for rejecting one, so the trade-off that the choice makes is not evaluated.

ADR 0001 requires a new tracked promotion boundary to evaluate commit order and recovery ownership. The selected promotion-recovery requirements introduce a new public recovery result and a rollback failure lifecycle. The only place that evaluates this, the spec's ADR Evaluation section, is not part of the Spec Requirement selection, and no selected text cites ADR 0001 or states a conclusion for this boundary, so the mandatory evaluation is absent from the selected scope.

The selected requirements add a protected read boundary that accepts a verified principal, evaluates an authorization policy and returns artifact bytes. The ADR conclusion for this security and authorization boundary is in the unselected ADR Evaluation section, so the selected requirements contain neither an applicable ADR reference nor an explicit no-ADR conclusion for it.

ADR 0004 requires runtime behavior to be tested through public lifecycle Interfaces. The promotion-runtime Testing Decisions state that request binding and retentionDays are internal preconditions that are not tested as public contracts and are checked only by source review. Request binding gates which artifact reaches persistence, so it is runtime behavior, and the selected text does not address this conflict with ADR 0004.

The authoritative retention source, ADR 0005, fixes only the duration of 30 days and says Readiness applies that policy without creating or changing it. The selected requirement adds a start point, 'from the successful tracked commit', which neither ADR 0005 nor rules/02 states. The spec therefore fixes a retention policy detail that its authority does not supply, so the start of the retained period cannot be verified against an authoritative source.

The Result Summary spec adds a caller-visible summary field to the promote successful result, and architecture/05 fixes that result as exactly {status, artifactId, trackedStateId} before this change. That changes a public Interface of the Promotion operation, so the document needs the complete Module Design format. It instead uses a Not required paragraph that says only that no runtime Module is added, so the format selection is wrong.

The Not required paragraph says only 'The parser optimization preserves the current architecture.' It does not state whether Module responsibility, Interface, Seam, dependency direction, authority or data flow is unchanged, and the cited requirement changes the internal parse flow to one forward pass that performs token recognition and field collection together. The reasoning is generic and does not establish that the change falls outside the categories that require the complete format.

Requirements say Readiness confirms the request binding before calling persistence, that Promotion trusts this precondition, and that Promotion adds no public parameter or failure branch. Module Design says the Promotion Module re-validates the request and artifact before persistence preconditions. Request validation therefore has two conflicting owners, and no section defines the caller-visible result when the binding check fails.

The ordered Invalid Input Diagnostic check for the recovery input is assigned to two modules: Promotion Module checks the input before handing it to Recovery, and Recovery Module applies the same ordered check to its public recoverPromotion(input) Interface. The validation policy therefore has two owners, and the spec does not say which owner's result a caller observes when both apply.

The Interface reviewAccess(request) accepts only the immutable request with resourceId and operation. The verified principal, which the security authority Input says is passed by the caller boundary together with the operation, has no input in the Interface. The Scope, Dependencies and Testing Decisions nevertheless depend on the principal, so the decision's authorization subject is not defined by any Interface input and the verified-principal test cannot be expressed against the Interface.

Testing Decisions require a Policy Adapter failure case through the public reviewAccess lifecycle, but no section defines its caller-visible result. Other Results define only invalid-policy, invalid-request and artifact-read-failed, and the Policy Evaluation Seam defines only the allowed, denied, invalid-policy and invalid-request results. The result for a failing policy adapter is therefore unspecified, and the required test cannot be verified as written.

The rollback failure result has one failureCode field, and the restore failure carries its own restoreFailureCode of 'restore-failed'. The Module section says Recovery keeps both the original commit failure and the restore failure, yet the spec does not say which code is the value of failureCode, and the other code has no caller-visible place. The failure result is therefore not fully specified.

The rollback failure result is a public recovery outcome with a defined shape and two possible baselineStatus values. The Testing Decisions cover only successful rollback and invalid input, so the rollback failure result, the retained baseline case and the preserved prior tracked state have no public lifecycle test and cannot be verified.

The Malformed Artifact Interface says Module uses the Invalid Artifact Contract validation order and reports the first invalid field, and that an extra field produces reason unexpected-field. The architecture's validation order (UTF-8, JSON syntax, root object, requestId, checks, then entry checks) does not place unexpected-field anywhere in that order. When an artifact has an extra field and another invalid field, the reported diagnostic is therefore undefined, and the multi-error test in Testing Decisions does not cover unexpected-field.

The Policy Evaluation Seam returns the allowed or denied decision, and both its production and deterministic adapters produce that decision. After the Seam returns allowed, the Access Review Module checks facts.operation against policy.allowedOperations as well. Operation membership is decided in two places with different owners, and the spec does not say which result governs when they disagree, or whether the Module may override an allowed result from the deterministic adapter.

The complete-format Dependencies and Data Flow section of promotion-recovery has no Source/Authority table. It describes Commit Failure Input, Rollback Command, Recovery Propagation and Remaining Baseline State in prose, so the declared authorities for the artifact, priorTrackedState, failedCommitId, commitFailureCode, restore result and baselineStatus are not listed in the required table.

The temporary baseline is written before the tracked commit. The spec defines its state only on failure paths, where rollback removes it and a failed expected write reports baselineStatus. After a successful tracked commit, the baseline's state (removed, retained or unspecified) is not defined, and no module is assigned that transition. The successful result also excludes its identity, so the lifecycle of this mutable state is incomplete.

The Boundary Alternative for the Access Review Module names only the chosen boundary, centralizing authorization policy evaluation, and its accepted cost. It names no alternative boundary, such as keeping authorization in the Artifact Reader or in the caller, and gives no reason for rejecting one, so the module boundary trade-off is not evaluated.
